items.title: DistroKid Removed Songs From Streaming Platforms in Response to UMG Copyright Suit
items.summary: Though the distributor was ostensibly targeting AI slop and potentially infringing content, numerous artists said their original music was hit with takedowns

items.title: Atlantic/WMG Sues Ray-Ban Owner Luxottica, Demands Over $64 Million in Damages as Social Media Infringement Crackdown Continues
items.summary: The social media copyright crackdown continues: Warner Music Group (WMG) is now suing multiple subsidiaries of eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica for allegedly infringing on north of 400 compositions and recordings in Instagram and TikTok posts. items.title: Italian Competition Watchdog Launches Suno Investigation ‘Over Unfair Terms,’ Says ‘The Contractual Provisions on Copyright Deserve Particular Attention’
items.summary: When it rains, it pours and, in Suno’s case, keeps on pouring: Besides facing a number of stateside lawsuits as well as international copyright claims, the AI music generator is now grappling with a formal investigation in Italy over its allegedly “unfair terms.” The Italian Competition Authority (ICA) disclosed the pr…

items.title: UK Copyright Tribunal ruling recognises “increased value of music in cinema” says PRS
items.summary: A dispute over what royalties cinemas should pay PRS for music contained in the films they screen went before the UK Copyright Tribunal earlier this year. It has ruled in favour of a higher royalty rate which, PRS says, “recognises the increased value of music in the overall cinema experience”

items.title: Sara Landry’s legal battle with ex-managers over commissions, copyrights and trademarks now being fought out in US and UK
items.summary: In August, London-based management firm The Night Department sued techno producer Sara Landry for breach of contract. She has now responded and countersued. The core dispute is over the management company’s involvement in her label, though there’s also some griping over a Coachella pissing incident

items.title: Major publishers tell US Supreme Court they must intervene in termination rights ruling that “threatens the licensing of copyrighted works throughout the world”
items.summary: The major music publishers and BMG have submitted a new filing with the US Supreme Court in the ongoing termination rights legal battle involving songwriter Cyril Vetter. He recently told the Supreme Court to ignore the publishers’ doomsaying about this case - their new filing has plenty of that

tip.title: Voz clonada: el derecho en juego suele no ser el copyright
tip.body: Imitar la voz de un artista con IA rara vez es infracción de copyright de la canción; el reclamo típico va por derechos de imagen, voz y publicidad, que varían mucho entre jurisdicciones.

tip.title: Cloned vocals: copyright is usually not the issue
tip.body: Mimicking an artist's voice with AI is rarely a copyright infringement of the song itself; claims typically run through name, image, voice and publicity rights, which vary widely by jurisdiction.
